title: end-to-end latency profiling traces - 2026-03-04 iter1
summary: Working notes for E2E latency trace collection and first-pass per-stage breakdown for short-text generation workload (seq_len ~128, tokens_out ~64). Goal: find p95 hotspots and validate batching/prefix cache efficiency.
body:
What we collected:
- 10k requests sampled from production-simulated workload (mixed small completions). Traces capture routing, queueing, batching, model-exec, kv-cache hits, decode, and postprocess.
- Env: Dedicated pool (A100s), runtime version v1.14.2, kernel profile: optimized-attn-2.
- Instrumentation: open-telemetry spans with stage tags; per-token emission timestamps for decode.

High-level numbers (aggregate across 10k requests):
- p50: 85ms
- p95: 260ms
- p99: 1.1s
- mean: 210ms
- error rate (5xx): 0.2% (not related to these traces)

Observations: 
- p50 is healthy and dominated by model-exec + decode.
- p95/p99 show significant tail caused by two factors: occasional large batch assembly delays (queueing) and model-exec NVLink stall when KV cache miss rates spike for long prefix requests.
- KV cache hit-rate for this sample: 78% overall, but for top-10 routes it is >95%; for low-frequency routes hit-rate falls to ~40%, correlating with long tail.

Per-stage breakdown (representative percentiles; times are medians of stage duration across requests at each percentile):
- ingress (HTTP parse/auth): p50 5ms | p95 9ms | p99 12ms
- routing/dispatch (policy selection + routing lookup): p50 4ms | p95 15ms | p99 40ms (spikes due to cache reloads and remote routing checks)
- queueing/batching wait: p50 2ms | p95 90ms | p99 420ms (high tail driven by bursty arrival patterns & strict batch thresholds)
- model-load/param fetch (cold host or reload): p50 0ms | p95 0ms | p99 120ms (rare but expensive)
- kv-cache lookup & prefix retrieval: p50 6ms | p95 18ms | p99 140ms (miss + remote fetch spikes)
- model-exec (attention + forward): p50 48ms | p95 85ms | p99 220ms
- decode (detokenize + streaming overhead): p50 12ms | p95 22ms | p99 50ms
- postprocess (safety checks, formatting): p50 3ms | p95 6ms | p99 9ms

Trace-level notes: 
- Long-tail requests (p99) typically have combination: routing spike (40ms) + batching wait (200-400ms) + kv-cache miss (100-200ms) => pushes total >1s.
- There is a recurring pattern where a small subset of routes (newly onboarded models/routes) have poor caching and cause higher latency; those routes show low prefix reuse and frequent small batches.
- When load increases, batching thresholds are reached less efficiently: we see FIFO queueing and some requests waiting to form an optimal batch, but bursty arrival leads to either small batches (higher per-token cost) or timeouts waiting for batch size.

Correlated signals we checked: 
- GPU utilization: 60-85% steady; spikes to 95% during heavy bursts but not sustained. No obvious straggler GPU compute times for same model shard.
- NVLink errors: none, but inter-node transfer latency occasionally increases during multi-tenant activity windows.
- Kernel timings: attention kernel variance contributes to p99 for long sequences; however in this workload seq_len is modest, so kernel variance is secondary.

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batching wait/config: batch formation thresholds and timeout policy produce high p95/p99 under bursty arrival patterns.
2) KV-cache miss hotspots for low-frequency routes cause remote fetchs and increase model-exec path by rehydrating prefix state.
3) Occasional model load/refreshes due to autoscaling or evictions cause rare >100ms spikes.
4) Routing service lookup (external calls) occasionally slow for specific route metadata keys.

Action items (short-term):
- A1: Lower max batch timeout by 10ms for small-size batches on Dedicated pool during peak hours; measure p95 change. Assignee: Noah. Due: 2026-03-09.
- A2: Add route-level cache metrics and alert when route-specific kv-cache hit-rate <60% for >1h. Assignee: Liu. Due: 2026-03-11.
- A3: Add synthetic spike tests (burst pattern generator) to reproduce queueing tails in staging. Assignee: Ava. Due: 2026-03-08.
- A4: Investigate routing lookup path; instrument external calls and add local route metadata cache with TTL. Assignee: infra-owner (TBD). Due: 2026-03-18.

Notes / next experiments: 
- Run controlled experiment varying batch_timeout at 5ms increments (0-50ms) with same arrival pattern; capture p50/p95/p99 and batch-size distribution.
- Rerun traces with kv-cache warm (artificially prime prefixes) to quantify KV miss penalty.
- Capture per-batch breakdown (time-to-first-token from batch assembly vs compute) to separate queueing from compute.

Quick reproducible run instructions (staging):
1) Deploy runtime v1.14.2 on staging dedicated pool (2 nodes) with same kernel profile.
2) Use workload generator script workload/synth/bursty-gen.py with seed set to 2026-03-03, target qps 120, mixture: 70% short completions, 20% medium, 10% long.
3) Enable trace sampling at 100% for the experiment window (10k requests).

Attachments: linked traces file (see linked_artifacts) and a short script to parse spans at scripts/parse_e2e_traces.py (WIP).

Informal notes (scratch):
- thinking: maybe adaptive batch timeout based on observed inter-arrival lambda could reduce tails without hurting throughput.
- we should surface route-level hit-rate on the console (ops -> route health).
- consider prefilling KV cache on route rollout to avoid early-miss spikes.
